content.value_statement: Modern Angular projects require clear choices across Signals, routing, rendering, and change detection. This skill provides practical patterns for building and modernizing Angular applications.
actual_capabilities: Designs local and shared state with Signals, computed values, effects, and RxJS interoperability.
Creates standalone components with signal inputs, outputs, models, queries, and direct imports.
Configures zoneless change detection, server rendering, hydration, and deferred loading patterns.
Applies functional routing with lazy components, guards, resolvers, and route data.
Structures dependency injection, reusable directives, forms, and signal-based stores.
Provides Angular testing and performance patterns for signal-driven components.
limitations: Targets modern Angular patterns and does not cover AngularJS migration.
Does not replace project-specific build, test, browser, or production validation.
Some future Angular features described in the source may require version verification.
Provides patterns and examples but does not inspect a project unless files are supplied.

use_cases.title: Start a modern Angular feature
use_cases.description: Plan a standalone, signal-driven feature with routing, state, and tests.

use_cases.title: Modernize an existing application
use_cases.description: Replace legacy Angular patterns gradually while preserving behavior and compatibility.

use_cases.title: Review Angular architecture
use_cases.description: Evaluate rendering, hydration, dependency injection, and performance choices before release.

prompt_templates.title: Create a signal component
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a standalone Angular component for [feature]. Use signal inputs and outputs, typed state, accessible markup, and focused tests.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Signals or RxJS
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Angular state flow: [details]. Recommend Signals, RxJS, or both. Explain ownership, async behavior, cleanup, and testing.

prompt_templates.title: Plan zoneless SSR
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a zoneless Angular SSR approach for [application]. Include hydration boundaries, deferred content, data transfer, failure states, and verification steps.

prompt_templates.title: Modernize an Angular codebase
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess these Angular files: [files]. Produce a phased modernization plan covering standalone APIs, Signals, routing, SSR, performance, compatibility, and regression tests.

output_examples.input: Design state for a searchable product list.
output: Keep products, loading state, and the search term in private writable signals.
Expose filtered products and loading status as read-only computed values.
Use HttpClient for the request and test success, error, and filter behavior.

output_examples.input: Review a dashboard route for lazy loading and access control.
output_examples.output: Use a fixed local lazy component import and a functional guard. Test authorized, unauthorized, and failed navigation paths.

output_examples.input: Prepare a page for server rendering and hydration.
output_examples.output: Enable client hydration, transfer server-fetched data, defer low-priority sections, and verify that server and client markup remain consistent.

best_practices: Confirm the installed Angular version before applying version-specific APIs.
Prefer incremental changes with focused build, test, rendering, and accessibility checks.
State data ownership, async boundaries, and error behavior before selecting Signals or RxJS.
anti_patterns: Do not force zoneless change detection into legacy code without compatibility testing.
Do not replace complex event streams with Signals when RxJS operators express the flow clearly.
Do not accept generated examples without checking imports, types, framework support, and tests.

faq.question: Which Angular versions does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets Angular 20 and later. Verify preview or future APIs against the installed version.

faq.question: Does it support AngularJS migration?
faq.answer: No. Use a dedicated AngularJS migration workflow for version 1.x applications.

faq.question: Can it help choose between Signals and RxJS?
faq.answer: Yes. It distinguishes local synchronous state from event streams, HTTP requests, and complex asynchronous flows.

faq.question: Does it cover server rendering?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers SSR setup, client hydration, incremental hydration, event replay, and transfer-state considerations.

faq.question: Can it update my project automatically?
faq.answer: It can propose and apply changes when project files and permissions are available. Builds and tests still require local validation.

faq.question: Does it include testing guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes TestBed patterns for standalone components, signal state, signal inputs, and DOM updates.
